name: TB Memory Pools & the Optical Fabric

pages.text: $(bold)Since 0.6.1 compute blades carry no memory at all.$() A blade is pure compute; memory moves into dedicated cabinets. That is not robbing Peter to pay Paul — it puts two costs on two meters: compute is bought in CWU/t, memory in TB.$(br2)A $(item)VRAM Storage Rack$() has 4 HBM slots:$(li)$(item)IV HBM Module$() — $(bold)4 TB$() each, $(bold)16 TB$() fully loaded;$(li)$(item)LuV HBM Module$() — $(bold)16 TB$() each, $(bold)64 TB$() fully loaded.

pages.title: 5×5×3 Memory Rack
pages.text: The VRAM rack casing plinth carries energy and maintenance. Mount a $(item)Datacenter Hardware Hatch$() on an exposed VRAM casing. Load its four slots with IV or LuV HBM from the hatch face. Pausing, removing HBM, failed maintenance or loss of power takes the rack out of the online memory pool.

pages.title: The 96 TB Training Gate
pages.text: The pretraining OOM gate rises to $(bold)96 TB$() in 0.6.1. The arithmetic is easy against the memory racks:$(li)one fully loaded LuV rack = 64 TB, $(bold)not enough$();$(li)$(bold)two fully loaded LuV racks = 128 TB, comfortably over$();$(li)or one LuV + two IV = 96 TB, exactly on the line.$(br2)If the pool is short the run $(bold)refuses to start$() with an explicit OOM instead of collapsing halfway.

pages.title: Hidden Wiring on Raised Floors
pages.text: Each machine’s entire base must rest directly on one connected $(item)Raised Floor$() rectangle. Every tile must be present. The short side must be at least 5, the long side at most 24, and the ratio at most 3:1. $(bold)6×6 and 18×8$() qualify. 1×12, 2×12, 5×20, holes and protruding strips invalidate the component.

pages.title: The 5×4×3 Backplane
pages.text: The plinth takes energy and maintenance. The cabinet casing also accepts up to four native computation receivers and four transmitters. The switch aggregates racks on its own floor and remote optical inputs. It offers up to $(bold)128 CWU/t$(). Over-bandwidth demand triggers $(bold)503$() for $(bold)300 ticks$().

pages.title: Cross-Room Optical Wiring
pages.text: Run GT optical pipe from the source $(item)Computation Transmitter Hatch$() to the destination $(item)Computation Receiver Hatch$(). Check both connections with a wrench. Use a room switch as the source to forward its memory pool as well as compute. Research Stations, scrubbing-tower inference hatches and other external consumers receive zero CWU/t when the pipe is absent or broken.
